text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- President Guntis Ulmanis and Prime Minister Andris Shkele have smoothed out differences and cleared the misunderstanding between them during a meeting. The president began talks with political parties to decide whether to nominate Shkele again or find another candidate.
- The nationalist Fatherland & Freedom faction, the third lartgest in the parliament, held talks with Ulmanis. It later decided to propose Economy Minister Guntar Krast as a new heaD of government.
- The three largest parliament factions believe the core of the government should still be formed by them: the Democratic Party Saimnieks, Latvia's Way and Fatherland & Freedom.

- Politicians are divided over the motives for Shkele's resignation. Ziedonis Chevers, head of Saimnieks, believes it is o result of scheming by intriguers hiding behind his party and says he intends to name them today. Others suggest the resignation was an attempt by Shkele to form a new cabinet on yet stricter conditions.
- New Russian ambassador, Alexander Udaltsov, arrived in Latvia. He is expected to hand in his credentials to Guntis Ulmanis on January 28.
DIENA

- Parliament speaker Alfred Chepanis, deputy speaker Andris Ameriks and the chairman of the parliament's budget and finance committee Robert Zile have left for Vienna to participate in a board meeting of Riga Commercial port.

- Former Finance Minister Aivars Kreituss and former parliament speaker Ilga Kreituse, his wife, plan to soon establish a new party - the Labour party - to defend the rights of employees. The new party will participate in the next general election, due in 1999.
- The number of Latvian Gas shares to be put on public offer will be increased to some 15 percent of the company's capital.

- Turnover at the Riga Stock exchange dropped more than half although prices mostly gained. Professionals believe the drop should not be explained by the resignation of the PM but by other market conditions.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The government approved rules for the certification of teachers.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- Businesses dealing in excise goods will have to apply for new licences at the newly established Excise Goods board.
SM
- This week Latvia is expected to sign an agreement with the St.Petersburg Quality certification centre on issuing quality certificates to Latvian food producers for 1997.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- The Bank of Latvia central bank reported a sharp increase in the amount of lats in circulation at the end of 1996. In December, currency in circulation increased from 262.8 million lats to 282.6 million lats.
-- Riga Newsroom, +371 721 5240
